thread.title: Special Participation E: DeepSeek as Web3 teacher
thread.content:
For special participation part E, I asked DeepSeek to teach me how to write a smart contract on BTC chain: https://chat.deepseek.com/share/9wu5248zp1z8hls9xyBased on our conversation, here is a summary in English of what I have accomplished and the current situation:Progress SummaryI have successfully completed the initial setup and are very close to deploying my first Bitcoin smart contract. Here is what I have done:✅ Environment Setup: I installed all prerequisite tools (Node.js, NPM, Git) on my Windows 11 computer.✅ Core Tools Installation: I installed the global CLI tool (@opcat-labs/cli-opcat) which is used to create and manage projects.✅ Project Creation: I created a new project named helloworld using the CLI. This command automatically generated the complete project structure and configuration files.✅ Project Dependencies (SDK): I entered the project directory and ran npm install. This installed all necessary dependencies for the project, including the crucial @opcat-labs/scrypt-ts-opcat SDK—the library containing the functions and classes needed to write my contract.✅ Smart Contract Code: I correctly modified the main contract file (src/contracts/helloworld.ts), creating a simple contract that stores a hash and can only be unlocked by providing the matching message.✅ Contract Compilation: I ran npm run compile, which successfully transformed my TypeScript code into a blockchain-readable format and generated a contract artifact file (artifacts/contracts/helloworld.json).✅ Test Key Generation: I generated a private key for the Bitcoin testnet using npm run genprivkey. The command provided I with a testnet address (mx79K19aq2Mq9mjUL1SHQ4y5NwTwcLKsFG) to receive faucet funds.Current Blocking IssueI am currently stuck at the final deployment step. When I run the deployment script (npx tsx deploy.ts), it fails with the following error:Error: Cannot find module 'D:\...\helloworld\dist\cjs\index.cjs'Analysis of the Problem: This is a technical configuration or compatibility issue, not a mistake in my following of the tutorial steps. The most likely causes are:Node.js Version Mismatch: I am using Node.js v22.20.0. The tools in this project (tsx and the SDK) may not be fully compatible with this very recent version and expect an older Long-Term Support (LTS) version like Node.js 18 or 20.Incomplete Build Process: The error points to a missing file in a dist directory. my npm run compile command compiled the sCrypt contract itself, but the deployment script may require the TypeScript project code to be compiled into a dist folder, which hasn't happened yet.Immediate Next Steps & SolutionTo resolve this and successfully deploy my contract, I need to:Add loadArtifact() to my Script: First, ensure my deploy.ts file includes the two critical lines that tell the system how to interact with my compiled contract. Add them after the other import statements:
import artifact from './artifacts/contracts/helloworld.json'
Helloworld.loadArtifact(artifact)
Switch to a Compatible Node.js Version (Recommended Solution): The most effective fix is to switch from Node.js v22 to an LTS version (v18 or v20). I can do this using a version manager like nvm-windows for Windows.Reinstall Dependencies & Recompile: After switching Node.js versions, go back to my project folder, delete the node_modules folder, and run npm install followed by npm run compile again to ensure everything is built correctly for the new environment.Once these steps are complete, funding my test address from the faucet and running npx tsx deploy.ts should successfully deploy and call my "Helloworld" smart contract on the Bitcoin testnet.In short: I have perfectly followed all tutorial steps. The final error is a common technical hurdle that is resolved by adjusting my Node.js version and verifying my deployment script's code.
thread.document:
For special participation part E, I asked DeepSeek to teach me how to write a smart contract on BTC chain: https://chat.deepseek.com/share/9wu5248zp1z8hls9xy

Based on our conversation, here is a summary in English of what I have accomplished and the current situation:

Progress Summary

I have successfully completed the initial setup and are very close to deploying my first Bitcoin smart contract. Here is what I have done:

✅ Environment Setup: I installed all prerequisite tools (Node.js, NPM, Git) on my Windows 11 computer.

✅ Core Tools Installation: I installed the global CLI tool (@opcat-labs/cli-opcat) which is used to create and manage projects.

✅ Project Creation: I created a new project named helloworld using the CLI. This command automatically generated the complete project structure and configuration files.

✅ Project Dependencies (SDK): I entered the project directory and ran npm install. This installed all necessary dependencies for the project, including the crucial @opcat-labs/scrypt-ts-opcat SDK—the library containing the functions and classes needed to write my contract.

✅ Smart Contract Code: I correctly modified the main contract file (src/contracts/helloworld.ts), creating a simple contract that stores a hash and can only be unlocked by providing the matching message.

✅ Contract Compilation: I ran npm run compile, which successfully transformed my TypeScript code into a blockchain-readable format and generated a contract artifact file (artifacts/contracts/helloworld.json).

✅ Test Key Generation: I generated a private key for the Bitcoin testnet using npm run genprivkey. The command provided I with a testnet address (mx79K19aq2Mq9mjUL1SHQ4y5NwTwcLKsFG) to receive faucet funds.

Current Blocking Issue

I am currently stuck at the final deployment step. When I run the deployment script (npx tsx deploy.ts), it fails with the following error:

Error: Cannot find module 'D:\...\helloworld\dist\cjs\index.cjs'

Analysis of the Problem: This is a technical configuration or compatibility issue, not a mistake in my following of the tutorial steps. The most likely causes are:

Node.js Version Mismatch: I am using Node.js v22.20.0. The tools in this project (tsx and the SDK) may not be fully compatible with this very recent version and expect an older Long-Term Support (LTS) version like Node.js 18 or 20.

Incomplete Build Process: The error points to a missing file in a dist directory. my npm run compile command compiled the sCrypt contract itself, but the deployment script may require the TypeScript project code to be compiled into a dist folder, which hasn't happened yet.

Immediate Next Steps & Solution

To resolve this and successfully deploy my contract, I need to:

Add loadArtifact() to my Script: First, ensure my deploy.ts file includes the two critical lines that tell the system how to interact with my compiled contract. Add them after the other import statements:

import artifact from './artifacts/contracts/helloworld.json'
Helloworld.loadArtifact(artifact)


Switch to a Compatible Node.js Version (Recommended Solution): The most effective fix is to switch from Node.js v22 to an LTS version (v18 or v20). I can do this using a version manager like nvm-windows for Windows.

Reinstall Dependencies & Recompile: After switching Node.js versions, go back to my project folder, delete the node_modules folder, and run npm install followed by npm run compile again to ensure everything is built correctly for the new environment.

Once these steps are complete, funding my test address from the faucet and running npx tsx deploy.ts should successfully deploy and call my "Helloworld" smart contract on the Bitcoin testnet.

In short: I have perfectly followed all tutorial steps. The final error is a common technical hurdle that is resolved by adjusting my Node.js version and verifying my deployment script's code.
